blocks.prompt: 2. Find a point on the curve \(y = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) - \frac{x}{3}\), where tangent is horizontal. Also find the equations of the tangent and normal at that point.
blocks.explanation:
Horizontal (leti hui) tangent ka matlab hai slope zero, is liye hum \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) solve karenge.
Diya kya hai? Curve \(y = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) - \frac{x}{3}\).
Find kya karna hai? Woh point, aur phir wahan tangent aur normal ki equations.
Rule kaunsa? \(m = 0\) ho to tangent \(y = y_0\) aur normal \(x = x_0\).
Plan: derivative, use zero ke barabar, \(x\) nikalo, curve se \(y\), phir dono lines.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right) - \frac{x}{3}\) ...(1).
Maloom karna: woh point jahan tangent horizontal hai, aur wahan tangent aur normal.
Tareeqa: horizontal tangent ka slope \(m = \frac{dy}{dx} = 0\) hota hai. Phir tangent \(y = y_0\) aur normal, jo us par perpendicular hai, khari line \(x = x_0\).

(1) ko differentiate karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{1 + \frac{x^{2}}{9}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{9 + x^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{9 - (9 + x^{2})}{3(9 + x^{2})}\]
\[= \dfrac{-x^{2}}{3(9 + x^{2})}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{d}{dx}\tan^{-1}u = \frac{1}{1 + u^{2}}\frac{du}{dx}\) mein \(u = \frac{x}{3}\), \(\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{3}\). \(\frac{1}{1 + x^{2}/9}\) ko upar neeche 9 se multiply kiya to \(\frac{9}{9 + x^{2}}\) bana, aur \(9 \times \frac{1}{3} = 3\). Phir dono fractions ka common denominator \(3(9 + x^{2})\) liya.
Dhyan dein: bracket \(-(9 + x^{2})\) kholte waqt dono terms ka sign badalta hai, isi liye 9 cancel hua.

Slope ko zero ke barabar rakhein
\[\dfrac{-x^{2}}{3(9 + x^{2})} = 0\]
\[x^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\]
Kyun: fraction tabhi zero hota hai jab upar wala (numerator) zero ho. Neeche wala \(3(9 + x^{2})\) kabhi zero nahi hota kyunke \(9 + x^{2} \ge 9\).

Point nikalein
\[y = \tan^{-1}0 - 0 = 0\]
To point \((0, 0)\) hai, yani origin.
Kyun: (1) mein \(x = 0\) rakha; \(\tan 0 = 0\) hai, is liye \(\tan^{-1}0 = 0\).
Dhyan dein: \(y\) hamesha asal curve (1) se nikalte hain, derivative se nahi. Derivative mein \(x = 0\) rakhne se to sirf slope 0 milta hai, point ka \(y\) nahi.

Tangent aur normal
Tangent (slope 0, point \((0, 0)\)):
\[y - 0 = 0(x - 0) \Rightarrow y = 0\]
Normal (\((0, 0)\) se guzarne wali khari line):
\[x = 0\]
Kyun: \(m = 0\) ho to formula \(-\frac{1}{m}\) nahi chalta (zero se divide), is liye seedha rule: tangent \(y = y_0\), normal \(x = x_0\). Yahan tangent \(x\)-axis hai aur normal \(y\)-axis.

Tasdeeq
\((0, 0)\) ko (1) mein rakhein: \(\tan^{-1}0 - 0 = 0\), theek. Aur \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{-x^{2}}{3(9 + x^{2})}\) har \(x\) ke liye zero ya negative hai, aur zero sirf \(x = 0\) par. Yani curve hamesha neeche ja raha hai aur sirf origin par ek lamhe ke liye seedha (level) hota hai. Is liye yahi akela point hai.
